projects.title: CyberResponse v2
projects.summary: Casework platform backend with AI agents.
projects.description:
Designed the backend around a core case API, wrapped by an MCP server that exposes 5+ case-management tools to Python workflows.

Enforced safe state transitions: every agent action passes schema validation and human approval before any case-state change.

projects.title: SciClaim
projects.summary: Scientific claim verification: hybrid retrieval, query rewriting, reranking and LLM-generated verdicts on SciFact.
projects.description:
A group project: a retrieval and generation pipeline that verifies scientific claims against the SciFact corpus.

Each claim is rewritten by Qwen3-1.7B into a sparse (BM25-friendly) query and a dense (semantic) query. BM25 and dense retrieval (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) are fused into 20 candidates, a cross-encoder (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) reranks them to the top 3, and an instruction-tuned model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct by default, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct as an alternative) produces a structured verdict: SUPPORTS, REFUTES or NOT ENOUGH INFO, with an evidence summary, reasoning and counter-evidence.

Retrieval and rewriting were evaluated with Recall and nDCG on the 300-query test set. Hybrid retrieval outperformed BM25, and BM25 outperformed dense retrieval, on every reported metric; both rewriting pipelines improved on their retrieval-only baselines. End-to-end verdict accuracy was 58% on a 50-query sample, with a mean latency of about 36 seconds on CPU and a 2% parse-failure rate.
highlights: Hybrid retrieval Recall@5 0.779 vs BM25 0.743 and dense 0.731 (300 queries)
Hybrid rewriting reached nDCG@5 0.707, above every retrieval-only baseline
Cross-encoder reranks 20 candidates to the top 3 evidence passages
Structured verdicts with evidence summary, reasoning and counter-evidence

projects.title: Qwen RAG Knowledge Assistant
projects.summary: Retrieval-augmented question answering with Qwen and Chroma, evaluated separately at the retrieval and answer stages.
projects.description:
A retrieval-augmented generation app built on SQuAD: documents are cleaned, chunked and embedded with a Qwen embedding model into a Chroma vector database, and a Qwen instruction model answers from the retrieved context only. A Gradio interface shows the answer together with its source chunks, so answers can be checked.

Retrieval and answers are evaluated separately. Vector retrieval found the correct answer in the top 5 chunks 92% of the time. A BM25 + vector hybrid with Reciprocal Rank Fusion helped some exact-keyword queries but did not improve overall accuracy on this set, so vector retrieval stays the default. On a small 10-question sample, answers reached 70% exact match and 90% containment.
highlights: Vector retrieval top-5 accuracy: 92%
Hybrid BM25 + vector search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion compared as an experiment
Answers shown with their source chunks
70% exact match and 90% containment on a 10-question sample

projects.title: ML Tutor LLM with LoRA
projects.summary: Fine-tuning a compact instruction model with SFT and LoRA to answer beginner machine learning questions.
projects.description:
A hands-on LLM workflow: instruction-response data is converted to chat format, a compact instruct model (SmolLM2-360M-Instruct) is fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning and LoRA, and the tuned model is compared against the base model. The LoRA adapter is saved, reloaded and served through a small command-line chat app.

It also explores decoding strategies (greedy, temperature, top-p) and inspects logits and next-token probabilities. It is a learning project with a deliberately small dataset, not a production model.
highlights: SFT + LoRA fine-tuning of SmolLM2-360M-Instruct
Base vs tuned model evaluation
Decoding strategies and next-token probabilities explored
Shipped embedding-based semantic job matching (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and pgvector) as the platform's core feature for 100+ candidates and recruiters, replacing keyword search across 500+ job listings.
Built the core backend in Java Spring Boot (20+ REST endpoints, PostgreSQL schema) calling a separate Python FastAPI embedding microservice, and documented the APIs with OpenAPI.
Worked in an Agile Scrum team, taking part in sprint planning, standups and code reviews on pull requests.

Owned debugging of a production latency issue: profiled with OpenTelemetry and Spring Boot Actuator, found pgvector search took 5 ms while an ORM N+1 query caused 850 ms, and cut p95 latency to 120 ms with JPA batch fetching.
Built fault-tolerant service calls between Spring Boot and FastAPI using Resilience4j circuit breakers and exponential backoff, with automatic fallback to PostgreSQL full-text search during outages.
Improved precision@5 by about 20% over the keyword baseline through evaluation, error analysis and 100+ test cases, and iterated the pipeline after user feedback revealed seniority-level mismatches.
Owned deployment of the services in Docker alongside React and Next.js UIs, and presented accuracy versus latency trade-offs to leadership, securing sign-off to launch matching as the core feature.
Replaced manual pre-release checks with GitLab CI/CD pipelines running automated test suites on every code change.
Built Java Selenium and TestNG regression suites covering 40+ workflows.
Validated 100K+ records in Python and SQL, catching 2,500+ data quality issues before they reached downstream systems.

research.title: A Multilingual Stroop Benchmark for Testing Visual-Textual Cue Interference in Vision-Language Models
research.summary: MSc dissertation (Queen Mary University of London). Tests whether vision-language models report the visible font colour in Stroop-style images or are pulled towards the written word or background colour. Evaluates CLIP ViT-B/16 and Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct across English, Chinese, Hindi and Arabic, with prompt-robustness and text-recognition controls, plus Grad-CAM-style and attention heatmaps for interpretability.
